punchline: Taleb's idea of playing it safe skips medium risk entirely: almost everything ultra-safe, a small slice wildly speculative.
thirty_sec: Taleb says you can't predict Black Swans, so stop trying and choose your exposure instead. His example is the barbell. Put roughly 85 to 90 percent of your money in the safest instruments you can find, and the rest in very speculative bets. Skip the medium-risk middle. That way a disaster can only take the small slice, but a lucky surprise can pay off big.
